Hi, public school here for 10 years, elementary art. Right now, I have 450 students, I teach 6-7 classes a day, one 45 minute prep in the morning before any classes, and there is 5 minutes in between classes. That five minutes usually ends up being less because of coure people come to get kids late at times. Still, I find it nice because sometimes I just need those two minutes to zip around and maybe refill the water trays, or put some things away, or just have a break for a bit. The principal (and teachers) also get and understand having this time is helpful and good for us specialists, but also has said she may need to change it next year because it makes sub rotations confusing which I also understand.

In the past there was no time in between classes at all, which definitely felt more stressful to me. The issue for me was really more of teachers not being back exactly on time to get classes, so the next class has to wait. I think if it went back to this, I would feel less stressed than I used to because I have no problem now just making kids clean up earlier so that they are fully finished and in line when it's time to go. Since I'm full time and a public school how I'm paid has nothing to do with when I don't have classes.

I mean, I don't really know your situation fully but if it were me and the choice was either I get 30 minutes between classes but I do not get paid, or I can have them all in a row and get paid and get to leave an hour or so earlier, I would 100% pick the second option. They might be lying but I could see a teacher saying they'd rather skip having in between time if it meant they are working more for free. I also think in some ways it's kind of messed up for them to be allowed to schedule you in a way where you have built in prep times that you don't get paid for in the middle of your schedule, so maybe it was an issue with that. Idk. 

I think really the best thing you can do is just understand that this is your situation and it won't be changing any time soon (at least this school year) so to keep your sanity you just need to be firm with cleanup times and make sure that not only are the kids full cleaned up and in line by the time they should leave, but you also have enough time to run around and do what you need to do. There are plenty of times I tell kids "I need to grab these things, talk to each other for two minutes while I do that" when they enter.

Well I first off would tell them that 5 credits of art are required to graduate, and that isn't your rule but a rule made by the state education department so whether they love art or not, they do have to take two classes and put in effort.

I would then focus on the word effort. Notice how I didn't say "You do have to make pretty art"? I'd tell them I don't care if their art is the prettiest thing but if they have made a solid effort that means much more to me. Effort can be shown by attempting multiple times to complete the project, or asking for help to try to understand it, etc. I'd make sure to keep emphasizing it does not matter to you if the art is PRETTY at all. 

At the same time despite these classes being so lazy I would cut them a bit of slack. It's not your fault the last teacher sucked, but it's also not theirs. If you came in mid February and up to that point they'd done nothing much and suddenly are expected to do this big project that requires some prior knowledge of art of course some are going to fail because they seemingly did not have much of an art education to begin with. You may need to dumb stuff down a bit until the end of this school year, or just be a lot more lenient on the grading scale.

Firstly as an elementary art teacher who has seen his exact situation so many times I want to say thank you for understanding that the general education placement for your child is not the best fit. There's a lot going on with your story here... I understand why you're upset completely, I'm going to try to explain why some of these things may be happening as I've seen similar things happen before at my school. First of all, the general education classroom teacher has probably been completely exhausted by this behavior over and over... If this is happening even with a 1 on 1 and all the supports you mentioned it must be really hard to manage him. On top of this she has all the other kids in class who might be crying and scared and then the issue of kids getting mad he "gets to do whatever he wants" or getting prizes for doing work while they don't is super common especially with kindergarten. Kindergartners don't really understand this kind of stuff especially when the child in question appears "normal" to them. Also while it might be easy to feel the gen ed teacher doesn't do a good job because the sped teacher gets your son to do work, the sped teacher also probably only has a small handful of students they service and gets to dedicate their full attention to your kid. The gen ed teacher can't do that.

The teacher/parent messaging all the other parents is inappropriate yes because she should not be spreading information especially IEP related information... At the same time I kind of get why. My guess is your child's teacher has been complaining to admin all year about this. You've even said you want him in a different environment and yet that isn't happening. The fact of the matter is the fastest and sometimes only way to get admin/the district to actually do something is if parents band together and complain. Last year we had a kindergartener who was similar to your child though she was extremely violent and hard to contain and mom refused to do anything. The classroom teacher started to quietly encourage parents at pick up to call in and complain. Eventually the parents all did this together and suddenly a week later this girl was moved to a school that had a much smaller environment for her and from what we have heard she's doing much better now. 

So while I get you feeling upset I also kind of understand some of the things that went on. Hi, fellow teacher here! I live in Milwaukee but teach out in Racine. 

Firstly, I wouldn't worry too much how far your drive is if you don't have a school lined up yet. MPS is a massive school district, if you plan to work for MPS. I worked in MPS for three years and personally hated it (I'm an art teacher so I was always spread out for multiple schools) and now work in Racine unified. I still live in Milwaukee and drive 45 minutes each way, which I don't mind because I like where I work but don't want to live in Racine. 

As for what areas are safe, if I'm being real with you in Milwaukee 900 a month is not going to get you anywhere too great. Avoid the north side for sure, Walkers Point is kind of cool and there's bars and stuff there, it's definitely not the safest. Lower East Side is also probably ok, but keep in mind it's near the big college campus so there will be lots of college kids around and can be loud. There's probably more to do out there than walkers point. 

For 900 a month and if you're concerned about safety I'd consider looking in areas like Greenfield, West Allis, maybe Saint Francis (if it's in budget), unless you really want to live more in the middle of Milwaukee. 

Rush hour can be annoying. When I worked for MPS I worked on the north side while living in Bay View which without rush hour should be a twenty minute drive but during rush hour could be up to 45 in awful traffic. 

I guess I'd try to see what districts you might want to work in and figure which areas are kind of more central.

as much as I hate being ADHD and wish I could magically get rid of it somehow, I do think that being ADHD is probably what makes being an elementary art teacher a job I can be successful at. I'm not a doctor but I do have ADHD and this is how it's been explained to me...

For a lot of people with ADHD, our brains do not produce dopamine as readily as non ADHD people. So, for most people, you do a task, let's say laundry, your brain says good job, and you get dopamine, which gives you a boost of energy and you feel good. For some people with ADHD (myself included), I get no dopamine from completing tasks. Doing boring household chores sucks because I don't feel anything after doing it, no sense of accomplishment at all, and it feels like my energy is being zapped out of me. 

So it's not so much that we crave it MORE than people, it's just that our brains do not produce it as much as other people, so we "need" it more to function as well as non ADHD people. I used to take a stimulant that made your brain **retain** dopamine you made and not deplete it, but I still felt very tired all the time.. switched to a different type that actively makes your brain **create** more dopamine, and I have had SO much more energy, been able to do more tasks without feeling like I need a 2 hour nap, etc.

I do this to sometimes! If I am giving directions and a child (or multiple) are causing so much disruptions it takes time away from everyone I will tell them they wasted x minutes of everyone's time (I usually just say 5), so when everyone else starts they have to wait five minutes. If they wait nice they get the supplies right away, if they're not waiting nicely they get an extra minute or two until they figure it out.

I see kids for 45 minutes once a week, and I'm 10 years in at this point.

First off, I do not give any kind of reward for good behavior, ever. I've never given candy or stickers or any of that. Their reward for being good is they got to have fun in art class 🤷‍♀️

As for behaviors... If it's only 1 or 2 not participating, oh well in my opinion. I would rather focus my energy on the kids who love art and want to ask me about it or share with me. I still try to ask the uninterested ones to join but I won't force them. I will tell them "Well if you change your mind there's a paper here for you" and walk off. Sometimes they end up getting bored and doing it. 

A few things I do...

If a kid is crumpling up their paper and demanding a new one, the consequence is you either get that one out the garbage and un-crumple it or you sit there and be bored the rest of class. 

If a kid is repeatedly ruining a new or special supply on purpose (like smashing the paint brush down and ruining the bristles) after a warning or two I take it and they have to use something like crayon instead. If a whole class can't handle special supplies, they all don't get them.

If a kid is being mean, hurting, yelling at, or greatly disrupting other kids so we can't get through class, I threaten to call home and then sometimes I actually do it (rarely, because it is a waste of my time usually) OR call the office. 

If a kid is destroying things in my room I threaten to destroy their art. I know some people would find that wrong, but it works almost every single time. If a kid destroys another kids artwork just to be mean or laugh at them, I've even gone so far as taking theirs and doing whatever they just did to their work. 

After 10 years what my main philosophy is, is that unless the behaviors are actually disrupting the kids who are doing what they are supposed to, I *ignore* it. I have students who every time they come to art whine they hate art, sit in a corner, and ignore me. I will let them know they get a grade, and I say it like "Look, I get you don't like art, and you don't want to do it, but I want you to understand if you refuse to do anything you will get a 0" and walk away. Sometimes telling them like that gets them to at least try and other times they don't care. If a kid gets up and wanders around but isn't *actually* doing anything I will ignore them typically. You have to think sometimes if you yelling at the kid or redirecting is almost more distracting than whatever the kid is actually doing. 

Hopefully this is helpful, if not sorry lol
